name: EXP-CLEAN-001 Delete the dead code and the legacy migration, and make the deletion stick
goal:
EXP-CLEAN-001 — Delete the dead code and the legacy migration, and make the deletion stick

OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-10-13, verbatim in substance): there are large blocks of code not being used
at all — dead code, dead imports — and the operator wants all of it gone, along with "this migrations
thing": a legacy migration one of the agents created when the project's structure changed, which the
operator has asked to have removed several times. Each request was verbal and each time the code was
still there afterwards.

WHY IT KEEPS COMING BACK — and therefore what this expedition must actually deliver
A removal that is only performed is a removal that can be undone by the next agent that finds the
code, cannot find a decision explaining why it should not exist, and concludes it is load-bearing.
Nothing in the repository currently records that `synth migrate` was asked to be deleted: there is no
ADR, no CHANGELOG entry, no guard test, and the compiler is not configured to notice dead code at all
(`noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are both absent from tsconfig.json, so the build is green
with 212 dead declarations in it). So deletion is HALF the work. The other half is three artifacts
that make re-introduction fail loudly: the two tsconfig flags, an ADR stating the decision and its
reason, and a chained removal-manifest test asserting the specific paths and names stay gone.

SEQUENCING (operator decision): this runs AFTER the testing work is addressed. Hard dependencies:
EXP-TEST-001 (e9a83ffda86ca767), EXP-TEST-002 (f6420030064a6f70), EXP-TEST-003 (328c0147b49d2743),
EXP-TEST-004 (a33ac4392da04d0e), EXP-TEST-005 (74c33996d5e7cf32), and EXP-CLI-003 (e47a186cb472a20a).
Rationale: EXP-CLI-003 restructures src/cli into a verb -> loader registry and repoints the test
harness; deleting modules underneath it would guarantee conflicts and would make its load-budget
measurements meaningless. EXP-TEST-005 decides which test files have owners, which determines whether
a "referenced only by tests" module is alive or orphaned — that verdict is an input here, not
something to guess at.

MEASURED INVENTORY (2026-10-13, branch arena/15e0fc51-synth at 21d3aba7, dist rebuilt from source;
every number below was measured, and each is labelled with how strong its evidence is)

D1. THE LEGACY MIGRATION — the operator's specific ask. 519 lines of source:
      src/cli/migrate.ts        260 lines   the `synth migrate` verb: detect, plan, archive, import
      src/migration/detect.ts   140 lines   detectLegacyState
      src/migration/plan.ts      80 lines   buildMigrationPlan, resolveLegacyEventLogPath
      src/migration/types.ts     39 lines
    Plus 12 references inside src/cli/synth.ts, and `migrate` is one of the 33 verbs in the canonical
    COMMANDS list in src/cli/usage.ts — so removing it is a public verb-surface change, not an
    internal cleanup. Evidence it is unused in practice: the 1572-invocation census of a full test run
    records exactly 4 `migrate` calls, and its only test (tests/migration.test.js) is a RED ORPHAN —
    not one of the 115 chain segments, and it currently fails with ENOENT on a temp archive directory
    (verified identical on both the pre- and post-Phase-0 builds, so it is pre-existing). Those 4 calls
    are that broken test. Nothing else in the repository invokes the verb.
    Also in scope, because it is the same confusion in a second place:
      docs/expeditions/EXP-MIGRATE-001.md, docs/governance/convergence-review-migrate-001.md,
      docs/guides/agents/migration-strategy.md,
      docs/guides/agents/migrating-runtime-data-to-synth.md,
      docs/reference/term-migration-report.md, docs/reference/terminology-migration-report.md
        — 1046 lines across 6 files
      examples/legacy-node/ (README.md, package.json, scripts/run.js) — 65 lines
    A DIFFERENT migration that must NOT be confused with the above:
      scripts/generate-npm-task-migration.js (128 lines) + tests/task-npm-migration.test.js (58 lines)
      generated the npm-script -> data/tasks migration. Its OUTPUT is load-bearing: 169 files in
      data/tasks/, including test:all.task.json, which is the canonical 115-segment chain that
      `npm run test:all`, `synth task run` and CI all execute. Neither the generator nor its test is
      chained, and no npm script references the generator, so the generator itself is now dead weight
      — but deleting it must not touch data/tasks/**, and `test:task-npm-adapter` (which IS chained) is
      a different thing again and stays.

D2. COMPILER-VERIFIED DEAD DECLARATIONS — the strongest evidence class, because tsc itself reports
    them. Running `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters -p tsconfig.json` on the current
    tree: **212 errors across 100 distinct src files**, while the normal build reports 0 errors only
    because both flags are absent from tsconfig.json.
      181 x TS6133  'x' is declared but its value is never read   (dead locals and dead imports)
       26 x TS6196  type declared but never used
        3 x TS6138  property declared but never read
        2 x TS6192  all imports in this line are unused
    Worst files: src/cli/synth.ts 17, src/cli/first-contact.ts 12, src/runtime/replay.ts 8,
    src/domain/execution.ts 8, src/cli/task.ts 7, src/adapters/repository/git.ts 5,
    src/signing/signer.ts 4, src/mission-studio/engine.ts 4.
    Note the interaction with EXP-CLI-003: 17 of the 212 are in synth.ts, which that expedition is
    decomposing. Fix these AFTER it lands, or the counts will have moved.

D3. MODULES UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SHIPPED ENTRY POINT — graph evidence, needs per-candidate proof.
    Transitive closure over static AND dynamic relative imports from the three entry points in
    package.json (bin.synth = dist/cli/entry.js, bin.synth-mcp = dist/distribution/mcp-server.js,
    main = dist/main.js): 304 of 348 dist modules are reachable, **44 are not — 2855 lines of
    compiled JS**, clustered (compiled lines): first-contact 881, environment 722 + providers 152,
    execution 421, cli 299, discovery 84, core 44, mutation 19, capabilities 16, documentation 16,
    types 13, planning 12. Largest: environment/rules.js 333, first-contact/experiment.js 316,
    cli/adapter.js 299, execution/runtime.js 287, environment/orchestrator.js 245,
    first-contact/patterns.js 239, first-contact/scenarios.js 197.
    These are CANDIDATES, not verdicts. Unreachable-from-bin does not equal dead: a module can be
    loaded through a computed specifier, imported directly by a test, be an entry point for a
    distribution artifact not listed in bin, or be reachable only from dist/cli/synth.js — which the
    test harness spawns for 1536 of 1572 invocations even though it is not the shipped bin.
    (dist/cli/synth.js must be added as a fourth root before any deletion decision; EXP-CLI-003
    decides whether it stays a compatibility entry.) An earlier attempt at this measurement in this
    session produced a false answer twice — once by counting a mention in docs/*.md as a reference,
    and once by matching module stems, so that "adapter" appeared to be referenced by 23 test files
    and 230 docs when the match was really adapter-catalog, adapter-registry, etc. Any tool used here
    must resolve real specifiers to real paths and must be spot-checked against a module known to be
    alive and a module known to be dead.

D4. EXPORTED SYMBOLS NEVER REFERENCED — heuristic, weakest evidence class, verify per symbol.
    401 exported functions/consts/classes/types/interfaces/enums in src/**/*.ts whose name appears in
    no other src file, no test and no script. Top files: src/discovery/types.ts 21,
    src/ledger/delivery.ts 17, src/cli/certification-runner.ts 11, src/mission-studio/types.ts 10,
    src/environment/rules.ts 9, src/ledger/writer.ts 9, src/compiler/type-checker.ts 8,
    src/governance/project-mission.ts 8. Known false-positive mechanisms: barrel re-exports
    (`export * from`), symbols reached as `sdk.foo` through a namespace import, and public API surface
    that is intentionally exported for consumers of the package rather than for this repository. A
    symbol that is only re-exported and never called is still dead, but proving that means following
    the barrel chain, not grepping a name.

D5. PUBLIC VERBS THE SUITE NEVER INVOKES — an operator decision, not a silent deletion.
    Of the 33 verbs in COMMANDS, 31 are invoked by the 1572-call census. Two are invoked zero times:
      approval  (src/cli/approval.ts, 155 lines, 3 references in synth.ts)
      intent    (no src/cli/intent.ts; handled inline in synth.ts, 3 references)
    Zero invocations is evidence about the test suite, not about users. Removing a public verb is a
    breaking change; the operator must decide each one explicitly, and `migrate` (D1) is the one case
    where the decision has already been made and repeated.

DELIVERABLES
  1. Remove the legacy migration (D1): the verb, src/migration/**, its 12 references in synth.ts, its
     entry in COMMANDS, tests/migration.test.js, the 6 docs (1046 lines) and examples/legacy-node.
     Decide the generator half of D1 separately and, if it goes, prove data/tasks/** and the
     115-segment chain are untouched by re-running `npm run test:all` before and after.
  2. Fix all 212 compiler-reported dead declarations (D2) and turn `noUnusedLocals` and
     `noUnusedParameters` ON in tsconfig.json permanently. This is the guard that makes dead imports
     fail the build instead of accumulating silently again.
  3. Resolve the 44 unreachable-module candidates (D3) to verdicts — delete, keep-with-reason, or
     keep-because-reachable-from-synth.js — using a resolver that survives the spot-check described
     above, and delete the ones proven dead.
  4. Resolve the 401 unused-export candidates (D4) the same way, following barrel chains.
  5. Put D5 to the operator as an explicit keep/remove decision per verb.
  6. Write ADR-057 (docs/adr/, next free number after ADR-056) recording WHAT was removed, WHY, WHO
     decided, and that re-introducing it requires reversing the ADR — plus a CHANGELOG.md entry for
     the removed public verb. This is the artifact whose absence caused the recurrence.
  7. Add a chained removal-manifest test asserting the deletions hold: no src/migration/**, no
     src/cli/migrate.ts, no `migrate` name in src/cli/usage.ts COMMANDS, no `synth migrate` in the
     help payload, no tests/migration.test.js, no docs/guides/agents/migration-strategy.md, no
     examples/legacy-node/**, and (if removed) no scripts/generate-npm-task-migration.js — while
     data/tasks/** and the chain length remain intact. Register it as a task and append it to
     test:all.task.json so it runs on every chain execution.

ACCEPTANCE
  * `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters -p tsconfig.json` exits 0, and both flags are
    present in tsconfig.json.
  * `synth migrate` no longer exists: the verb is absent from COMMANDS, `synth help` does not list it,
    and invoking it produces the standard unknown-command envelope. `synth --help` still lists every
    remaining verb and both entry points stay byte-identical across the nine-invocation surface that
    tests/loader-entrypoint.test.js guards.
  * The removal-manifest test is a chain segment and passes; deliberately re-adding one removed path
    makes it fail (proved, then reverted).
  * `npm run test:all` stays green and its segment count is the pre-change count plus the new
    manifest test, minus any removed migration test task. No currently-green orphan turns red. The
    four known pre-existing red orphans (synth-cli-repo, migration, first-contact-cli,
    governance-report-cli) are accounted for explicitly — note that removing tests/migration.test.js
    retires one of them rather than fixing it, and the evidence must say so instead of letting the
    red count silently drop.
  * `synth verify` ok; `synth doctor` 12/12; `synth log`/`checkpoint` still report real counts and
    layouts (at the time of writing: 473 events, segmented layout).
  * Every deletion in the evidence is labelled with its evidence class — compiler-verified,
    graph-reachable, census-backed, or heuristic — and every heuristic deletion names the check that
    confirmed it. Line counts removed are reported per category, with the source line total and the
    compiled-JS total given separately.
  * dist-manifest, determinism and proof re-baselined deliberately, with the new file count and
    rootHash stated (at the time of writing: 1050 files, rootHash 3a59324b...).

NON-GOALS
  * Not the test inventory or file-ownership guard (EXP-TEST-005), not suite merging (EXP-TEST-002),
    not the sharded runner (EXP-TEST-003), not the logging/failure envelope (EXP-TEST-001), not
    explicit-environment fields (EXP-TEST-004). Where a module is alive only because an orphaned test
    imports it, the verdict waits for EXP-TEST-005 rather than pre-empting it.
  * Not the CLI decomposition, the load budgets or the dispatcher graph (EXP-CLI-003). This
    expedition deletes what is left after that restructuring, not instead of it.
  * No output-contract changes beyond the removal of the `migrate` verb. The four operator decisions
    settled in EXP-CLI-001 (JSON envelope for --version with --human for the bare string; no status
    INFO line on stderr; TTY-aware help; one unified verb list) stay exactly as they are.
  * Not the four source-path guard tests (tests/verify-engine, tests/artifact-policy,
    tests/governance-orchestration, tests/impact-analyzer), which reference src/cli/synth.ts by path
    and must never be deleted.
  * Not deleting data/tasks/** or anything the 115-segment chain executes.
